case_title: Deny Bora v. State of Assam
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.34; TADA s.314 (as stated in judgment; accused acquitted of TADA offences)
evidence_type: Eyewitness (PW-14, sole testimony implicating accused); medical (post-mortem report, PW-17)
trial_court_outcome: Acquitted under TADA; convicted under IPC s.302 and sentenced to rigorous imprisonment for life with fine of Rs.50,000, in default five years further rigorous imprisonment
high_court_outcome: Not applicable (appeal under TADA s.19 came directly to the Supreme Court)
neutral_facts: On the evening of 2 March 1991, the victim, a medical practitioner, was attending patients in a clinic when two unidentified youths shot the victim from point-blank range, and the victim died. A report of the incident was lodged the following day. During the investigation, several witnesses who had heard about the occurrence from the victim's wife and daughter were examined. The post-mortem examination recorded two bullet wounds, one on the right side of the face near the outer corner of the eye and one on the left side of the neck just below the ear, and gave shock and haemorrhage from the bullet injuries as the cause of death. The victim's daughter had been with the victim at the clinic and was an eyewitness, while the victim's wife was slightly away from the scene. The eyewitness gave a statement to the investigating officers about two years and eight months after the incident. He stated that he had been threatened by a co-accused. His acquaintance with the accused was a fortnight old when he accompanied the accused and another person to the clinic, where the other person went inside pretending to be a patient. He asserted that the accused fired at the victim, who fell and died. The accused was arrested about eight years after the incident, following the eyewitness's statement. The victim's wife and daughter were not examined as witnesses.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from two gunshot wounds (right side of face near outer angle of right eye; left side of neck below the ear)
number_of_offences: 3 sections charged (IPC s.302, IPC s.34, TADA s.314 as stated; the judgment's '8 offences' count is unclear); 0 finally upheld
key_evidence_accepted: Post-mortem evidence establishing homicidal death from firing at point-blank range. The eyewitness testimony of PW-14 was not accepted as reliable.
witness_credibility: PW-14 (eyewitness): found thoroughly and wholly unreliable because of the two years eight months delay, the implausible threat explanation, and the implausibility of silence after witnessing the shooting. Wife and daughter, the most natural witnesses, were not examined and no explanation was given.
trial_duration: offence: 2.3.1991; trial judgment: 02.03.2013; High Court: not given; Supreme Court: 27.08.2014
legal_representation: Accused (appellant): P.K. Goswami, A. Henry, Vikas Singh. State of Assam (respondent): Navnit Kumar, Corporate Law Group
investigation_status: FIR registered 3.3.1991; accused arrested 20.02.1999; charge sheet filed 29.07.2001; trial completed with judgment 02.03.2013
procedural_irregularity: Non-examination of wife and daughter (present at or near scene) without explanation; eyewitness statement recorded about two years and eight months after the incident
appeal_history: Trial court (Designated Court, Guwahati): acquitted under TADA, convicted under IPC s.302, life imprisonment. High Court: not applicable (direct appeal to Supreme Court). Supreme Court: appeal allowed, conviction set aside.
prosecution_argument: PW-14's delayed disclosure was explained by threats from the co-accused, and witnesses may behave peculiarly, so his evidence is reliable and the conviction should stand
defence_argument: A conviction on a single witness needs absolute reliability; PW-14's delay and threat plea make his account incredible; non-examination of wife and daughter without explanation creates a dent; post-mortem report was impermissibly treated as proof of guilt
legal_principle_applied: Conviction may rest on a single witness if wholly reliable (s.134 Evidence Act), but corroboration is required where doubts exist; non-examination of material witnesses assessed by trustworthiness of evidence and whether they were the only competent witnesses
precedent_relied_upon: State of H.P. v. Gian Chand (2001) 6 SCC 71; Surinder Kumar v. State of Haryana (2011) 10 SCC 173; Takhaji Hiraji v. Thakore Kubersing Chamansing (2001) 6 SCC 145; Dahari v. State of U.P. (2012) 10 SCC 256; Sunil Kumar v. State (Govt. of NCT of Delhi) (2003) 3 SCC 169; Namdeo v. State of Maharashtra (2007) 14 SCC 150
other_sentence_order: Direction that the accused be set at liberty forthwith unless detention is required in connection with any other case
